prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on your needs (solo individual vs. small-business group, in-person vs. online, need for subsidy help, budget, desired carriers). Instead of naming one firm I don’t know your priorities for, here’s a fast, practical way to get the right broker in Kansas City — plus what to look for and ask.

Quick questions so I can recommend specific brokers:
- Are you buying an individual/ family plan or a small-business/group plan for employees?
- Do you need help qualifying for ACA subsidies (income varies year to year)?
- Do you prefer somebody local/in-person or are you fine with an online broker?
- Zip code (KC is large) and any special coverage needs (medications, specialists, dental, etc.)?

How to find a great broker in KC
1. Use reputable directories:
   - NAHU’s “Find an Agent” (national association of health underwriters).
   - Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance to verify licensing.
   - Healthcare.gov agents/brokers list if you want marketplace enrollment and subsidy help.
   - Read Google/Yelp/BBB reviews for local reputations.

2. Shop and interview three brokers (compare answers and responsiveness).

Important questions to ask any broker
- Are you licensed in Missouri? Can you show your license number?
- Do you specialize in individual & family plans, ACA marketplace plans, or small employer/group plans?
- How many self-employed clients do you serve? Can you provide references?
- Do you work with multiple carriers (independent) or only one carrier (captive)?
- What are your fees? (Many are paid by insurers; some charge a broker fee.)
- Will you help me determine subsidy eligibility and complete the marketplace application?
- Do you assist with year-round issues (claims, renewals, changes) and tax forms (1095)?
- Do you offer comparisons of total cost (premiums + deductibles + copays) not just premiums?
- What’s your enrollment turnaround and communication method (phone, email, in-person)?

What to expect for a self-employed person
- If you want tax credits/subsidies, you must enroll through the ACA marketplace (Healthcare.gov for Missouri) — confirm the broker can do that.
- If you want a short-term plan or off-exchange plan, subsidies won’t apply.
- Brokers should help estimate Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) for subsidy sizing — important for variable freelance income.
- If you have employees and want a group plan, requirements and options change; tell the broker how many employees and payroll frequency.

Next steps I can do for you
- If you give your ZIP code and preference (local vs online, individual vs group), I’ll suggest several Kansas City brokers and give a short pros/cons list and contact tips.
- Or I can draft an email/phone script you can use to contact brokers.

If you tell me zip code and whether you want in-person help or are OK with online-only, I’ll look up a short list of well-rated options and what to expect from each.
